comment: Single source of truth for the @mandusec/mandu bundle (packaging.md §5). `services` are the spawnable processes (the `ps` title minus the `mandu-` prefix, per runtime-instances.md §7); `modules` are bundled-but-imported (the arbiter IPC client the interceptors dynamic-import) or loaded beside a bundle (the arbiter's secret-discovery worker thread, which dist/arbiter.mjs starts from dist/secret-discovery-worker.mjs). build-bundle.mjs esbuilds every entry into dist/<name>.mjs; the launcher's layout resolver reads `services` to spawn `node dist/<name>.mjs` (installed) vs the from-source entry (dev), and points MANDU_ARBITER_CLIENT_MODULE at dist/arbiter-client.mjs. `assets` are static files copied VERBATIM to dist/<key> (the AppArmor userns grants `mandu setup` installs; rootless-confinement-ubuntu-2404.md §3.2; the SDK route preload a host program's Node loads and the permission-mode rule beside it that the preload requires, agent-sdks.md; the reference prompt classifier and its pack writer, which `mandu policy classifier-pack` runs, confidentiality-plan-15-prompt-filter.md §13.5) and resolved by Layout.asset(). `native` are the prebuilt Rust supervisor bins copied from $MANDU_NATIVE_BIN_DIR (default interceptors/target/release) to dist/native/<platform>-<arch>/<name> when they are built (services/native-bins.ts resolves them; the guard among them is what confines a no-userns host, plan 10 §11.7); a bin that is not built is skipped with a note, never an error. Entry paths are relative to the repo root. `optionalModules` and `optionalAssetDirs` are built and copied like `modules` and `assetDirs` when their source exists, and skipped with a note when it does not: the dashboard's developer view (dist/dashboard-dev.mjs, which dist/dashboard.mjs loads when it is there, and its pages under dist/dashboard/dev; dashboard.md §4.25ac). A build from the public tree has neither, so the package it makes serves the product page only.
